citation: Glessner House Museum, 'Burley & Tyrrell, Chicago's Forgotten Retailer', The Story of a House (blog), 18 January 2022; with an undated photograph of the John Tyrrell house, 1720 S. Prairie Avenue, photographer and holder not named.
author: Glessner House Museum
repository: The photograph is the Prairie library's image a16-ghm-blog-1720-tyrrell-house (stream-1600-1700), held in the image store as a reference copy.
locator: The paragraph on Tyrrell's house and the photograph of it.
rights_note: A museum's blog post, cited in words only; the photograph's holder and rights are not stated, so nothing is derived from it.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-19 (T-2642) from the live page; the photograph read from the image store's copy, 1200 x 1119 px, sha256 8bcc2366a0f42187342eb728565c1e9f4f174181977230ce70aebda733719b81, which the page shows.
note: Read: 'In 1868, Tyrrell purchased a large lot on South Prairie Avenue and engaged architect Otis L. Wheelock to design a substantial two-story frame house in the Italianate style. (He sold the house at 1720 S. Prairie in 1878 ...)'. The photograph shows the clapboard front: wide eaves on carved brackets, a low gable over the middle, round-arched windows under hood mouldings, single and paired, a canted bay at one front corner, and a full-width porch on paired posts with a central stair.
what_it_supplies: the style, the architect and the year
the front as photographed: brackets, centre gable, hooded arched windows, corner bay, porch
